t.1.99.1: Bhīṣma said: Mother, I shall tell you once more a sure means for increasing the offspring of Bharata's line; hear it from me as I speak.
t.1.99.2: Let some virtuous brāhmaṇa be invited with an offer of wealth, one who might beget offspring in the fields of Vicitravīrya.
t.1.99.3: Then Satyavatī, as if laughing, spoke these words to Bhīṣma bashfully, in a faltering voice.
t.1.99.4: What you say is true, mighty-armed Bhārata. Out of trust in you I shall speak, for the continuation of our lineage. It is impossible not to tell you, for this calamity is of such a kind.
t.1.99.5: You alone are dharma in our family, you are truth, you are the highest refuge. Therefore, having heard my words, do what must follow.
t.1.99.7: Then the wise Parāśara, the supreme seer and foremost of the upholders of dharma, came to the boat, intending to cross the river Yamunā.
t.1.99.6: O righteous one, my father, who was devoted to dharma, kept a ferry-boat. Once, in the first bloom of my youth, I went there.
t.1.99.8: As he was being ferried across the Yamunā, that best of sages, tormented by desire, approached me and then, beginning with soothing words, spoke to me much that was sweet.
t.1.99.9: Afraid of his curse and afraid of my father, O Bhārata, and addressed by him with boons hard to obtain, I could not bring myself to refuse him.
t.1.99.11: Formerly I had a strong fishy smell, which was loathsome; that sage took it away and gave me this pleasant fragrance.
t.1.99.10: Overpowering me, a young girl, with his splendor, he brought me under his control, O Bhārata, having covered the world with darkness while I was still in the boat.
t.1.99.12: Then that sage said to me: "Having brought forth my child on an island of this very river, you shall still be a maiden."
t.1.99.13: That son of Parāśara, a great yogin, became a great seer; born to me long ago when I was a maiden, he is known as Dvaipāyana.
t.1.99.14: The blessed seer who, by the power of his austerity, divided the four Vedas, attained in the world the name Vyāsa, and from his dark complexion the name Kṛṣṇa as well.
t.1.99.15: Truthful, devoted to tranquility, an ascetic whose sins are burnt away, he, when appointed by me and by you, O man of boundless splendor, will surely beget auspicious offspring in his brother's fields.
t.1.99.16: For he told me there, "Think of me when there are tasks to be done." I shall think of him, O mighty-armed Bhīṣma, if you so wish.
t.1.99.17: For with your consent, Bhīṣma, that great ascetic will surely beget sons in the fields of Vicitravīrya.
t.1.99.19: He who, having reflected rightly with his intellect upon wealth and what follows from wealth, upon dharma and what follows from dharma, upon desire and what follows from desire, and upon their opposites, each one separately, then makes his decision, he is wise.
t.1.99.18: When that great seer was named, Bhīṣma, his palms joined in reverence, said: "He who discerns these three, dharma, artha and kāma, …"
t.1.99.21: Then, O delight of the Kurus, when that had been agreed to by Bhīṣma, Kālī called to mind the sage Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana.
t.1.99.20: What you, my lady, have said is both in keeping with dharma and truly beneficial to our family; it is the highest good, and it pleases me.
t.1.99.22: Expounding the Vedas, that wise one, having perceived his mother's thought, appeared unseen in an instant, O delight of the Kurus.
t.1.99.23: Then, having offered worship to her son according to the prescribed rite, having embraced him with both arms and bathed him with the milk flowing from her breasts, the fisherman's daughter shed tears on seeing that son after so long a time.
t.1.99.24: Having sprinkled his distressed mother with water and saluted her, the great seer Vyāsa, her firstborn son, spoke these words.
t.1.99.26: Then the family priest offered worship to that supreme seer, and he accepted it in accordance with the rites, accompanied by sacred mantras.
t.1.99.25: Whatever is desired by you, that I have come to do. Command me, O you who know the true essence of dharma; let me do what is pleasing to you.
t.1.99.27: When he was seated, his mother Satyavatī asked after his lasting welfare; then, looking at him, she spoke these words immediately afterward.
t.1.99.28: Sons are born as the common possession of mother and father, O sage; just as the father is their master, so too is the mother, there is no doubt.
t.1.99.29: Just as you, ordained by the Creator, are my firstborn son, O brahmarṣi, so Vicitravīrya is my younger son.
t.1.99.30: Just as Bhīṣma is the brother of Vicitravīrya through his father, so too are you his brother through your mother, or however you yourself regard it, my son.
t.1.99.31: This son of Śaṃtanu, whose valor lies in truth, keeping true to his vow, sets his mind neither on offspring nor on ruling the kingdom.
t.1.99.33: Out of compassion, and for the protection of all beings, whatever I may say with kindness, having heard it, you ought to do.
t.1.99.32: So you, O sinless one, out of regard for your brother and for the continuation of the lineage, at the word of this Bhīṣma and at my command,
t.1.99.34: The two wives of your younger brother, O Bhārata, are like daughters of the gods, endowed with beauty and youth, and they long for sons.
t.1.99.36: Vyāsa said: You know the dharma, Satyavatī, both the higher and the lower; and likewise, O knower of dharma, your mind is fixed upon dharma.
t.1.99.37: Therefore, at your command, keeping dharma in view as the reason, I shall do what you desire, for this has been seen of old.
t.1.99.35: Beget offspring on those two, dear son, for you are capable: offspring worthy of this family, for the continuance and propagation of its line.
t.1.99.38: I shall give my brother sons equal to Mitra and Varuṇa. Let those two queens observe the vow that I have prescribed here.
t.1.99.39: For a year, as is proper, let them observe this vow; then they will be purified. For no woman who has not undertaken the vow may approach me.
t.1.99.40: Act so that the queen may conceive a child at once. In kingdoms without a king there is no rain, nor are there gods.
t.1.99.41: How can a kingdom without a king be sustained, O lord? Therefore beget an embryo; Bhīṣma will raise it.
t.1.99.42: If a son is to be given by me quickly, out of due season, then let her bear my ugliness; that shall be her supreme vow.
t.1.99.43: If Kausalyā can bear my smell, my appearance, my garb and my body, then let her this very day conceive an excellent child.
t.1.99.44: Saying this, the sage, eager for the union, vanished. Then the queen went to her daughter-in-law, whom she met in private, and spoke to her words that were righteous, meaningful and beneficial.
t.1.99.45: Kausalyā, understand from me what I tell you, which accords with the rule of dharma: clearly the Bharatas face extinction because my good fortune has run out.
t.1.99.46: Seeing me distressed and the ancestral line afflicted, Bhīṣma gave me counsel in this matter, for the furtherance of dharma as well.
t.1.99.48: O fair-hipped one, bring forth a son whose splendor equals that of the king of the gods, for he will bear the heavy yoke of kingship of our lineage.
t.1.99.47: And that decision rests with you, daughter; I have understood it. Raise up once again the ruined lineage of the Bhāratas.
t.1.99.49: Having somehow persuaded her, that follower of dharma, by appeal to dharma, she fed the brahmins, the divine seers, and the guests as well.
